analysis.title: Sector Flows Flash Update: Tech's Reversal of Fortune
key_insights: Citi's two-month, long-only-driven flow model still assigns its largest positive weights to Tech, Communications and Health Care, with Materials and Industrials modestly favored and Energy roughly neutral.
Financials and Consumer Discretionary remain the largest negative weights. Utilities has moved up to complete the bottom three, displacing Consumer Staples from the prior publication.

In the latest week both long-only and hedge fund managers turned decisively against Tech after weeks of buying. This lines up with the broader AI-related selloff, as investors reassess data center financing and capex against slower-than-expected AI revenue.

Long-only Tech selling in the latest week was the largest single move, in either direction, across all sectors. Hedge funds followed a similar arc, buying early in the window and then selling through the latest week.

Tech's favorable two-month model ranking is being driven by flows earlier in the window rather than the most recent weeks. In the combined one-month flows, Health Care and Tech were modest net sellers.

Communications and Consumer Discretionary registered the strongest combined one-month net inflows. Hedge funds were consistent buyers of Communications across the window and bought Consumer Discretionary steadily, while long-only flows in Consumer Discretionary were more mixed.

Health Care saw a late-stage reversal among hedge funds, which bought earlier in the window and sold significantly in the latest week. Long-only managers stayed modest net buyers of Health Care that week.
Financials long-only flows were volatile and included one of the largest single-week inflows of the period. Utilities, Real Estate and Materials flows were comparatively muted for both manager types.

Trailing one-month relative returns are led by Consumer Staples and Energy, with Health Care and Consumer Discretionary modestly positive. Tech, Communications, Financials, Industrials and Real Estate underperformed, a reversal from the prior report when Tech outperformed.

Sector returns have moved Citi's regime model toward Tightening Financial Conditions and Stagflation readings and away from Goldilocks. Citi had already flagged the prior Goldilocks signal as sitting uneasily with the rate backdrop and macro environment.
